headline: Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 9th meeting of CSMC
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 9th meeting of CSMC

Over 29,000 additional houses approved under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0, total sanctions now at 18.77 Lakh

11 SEP 2026 10:01PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has approved a total of 18.77 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0), giving further impetus to the implementation of scheme and accelerating progress towards ‘Housing for All’ in urban areas. The decision was taken in the 9th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA in New Delhi on 10th September 2026.

The meeting was also attended by Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary & Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA), Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary & Financial Advisor (JS&FA), senior officials from the Ministry and Mission Directors of from participating States. In today’s meeting over 29,000 houses were approved under Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0, covering six States - Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Telangana, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh.

Addressing the States, Secretary, UD (MoHUA), said that concerted efforts towards the timely and effective implementation, monitoring of PMAY-U 2.0 should be ensured so that the benefits of scheme reach all eligible beneficiaries. He further added that any bottlenecks should be promptly identified and addressed in consultation with the States/UTs.

Secretary, UD categorically mentioned that CSMC meetings will be convened every second week of the month to ensure regular monitoring and provide further impetus to the pace of progress of PMAY-U 2.0. He emphasised on States/UTs to submit the duly approved projects by end of each month for their timely consideration and sanction in the subsequent CSMC meetings.

Over 18 lakh families being benefitted

PMAY-U 2.0 seeks to provide housing assistance to eligible urban EWS/LIG and MIG families through its different verticals. Under the scheme, beneficiaries can construct their own pucca house, purchase a house in projects constructed under the scheme, avail affordable rental housing, or benefit from interest subsidy on eligible housing loans, providing a range of housing solutions suited to their needs, eligibility and financial circumstances.

With total 18.77 lakh approved under PMAY-U 2.0, the scheme is steadily expanding access to safe, affordable and pucca homes. These approvals mark a significant step towards ‘Housing for All’, enabling more urban families to move closer to owning a secure home and building a better future.

Major push towards ‘Housing for All’

PMAY-U 2.0 builds on the sustained progress made under PMAY-U. Overall, under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, more than 1.25 crore houses have been sanctioned and over 1 crore houses completed and delivered to beneficiaries.

Housing as a foundation for dignity and empowerment

The scheme caters to the housing needs of EWS/LIG and MIG families, having an annual household income of up to ₹9 lakh, enabling them to transition from kutcha, inadequate or rented accomodation to safe and dignified homes. By enabling vulnerable families to access adequate housing, the scheme has given them a renewed sense of security and stability, while helping them move towards a better quality of life.

The scheme also places strong emphasis on women’s ownership of houses. Houses sanctioned under the scheme are either in the name of woman of the house or in joint ownership, strengthening women’s economic and social position within the household. Of the 18.77 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0, 17.19 lakh houses (92%) have been allotted to women.

Further, to ensure inclusivity and extend the benefits of the scheme to vulnerable sections of society, 1.80 lakh houses have been allotted to senior citizens. 3.25 lakh houses have been sanctioned for SC beneficiaries, 1.02 lakh for ST beneficiaries and 8.22 lakh for OBC beneficiaries, reaffirming the scheme’s commitment to equitable access to safe, affordable and dignified housing.

With the cumulative number of PMAY-U 2.0 sanctions now approaching the 20-lakh milestone, the Government continues to work towards ensuring that every eligible urban family has a house to call their own. Each house sanctioned represents a family moving closer to a safer, more secure and dignified future.

(Release ID: 2309343)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) approved over 29,000 additional houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) during the 9th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), bringing total sanctions under the scheme to 18.77 lakh.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Meeting Details:** 9th CSMC meeting chaired by Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA, held in New Delhi on 10th September 2026.
- **New Approvals:** 29,000+ houses sanctioned under Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals across six states: Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Telangana, Tripura, and Uttar Pradesh.
- **Cumulative Sanctions:** Total houses approved under PMAY-U 2.0 now stand at 18.77 lakh.
- **Overall Scheme Progress:** Combined sanctions under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 exceed 1.25 crore houses, with over 1 crore houses completed and delivered.
- **Future Monitoring Cadence:** CSMC meetings will be convened every second week of the month; States/UTs directed to submit duly approved projects by end of each month for timely sanction.
- **Beneficiary Demographics (PMAY-U 2.0):**
  - Target groups: Urban EWS/LIG and MIG families with annual household income up to ₹9 lakh.
  - Women ownership: 17.19 lakh houses (92%) allotted to women (sole or joint ownership).
  - Senior citizens: 1.80 lakh houses allotted.
  - Social categories: 3.25 lakh (SC), 1.02 lakh (ST), and 8.22 lakh (OBC) houses sanctioned.

headline: Cochin Shipyard Ltd and Drydocks World Form Joint Venture To Strengthen India’s Ship Repair Industry
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Cochin Shipyard Ltd and Drydocks World Form Joint Venture To Strengthen India’s Ship Repair Industry

50:50 JV to operate & expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) in Cochin, strengthen India’s ship repair ecosystem, serve growing regional & global demand

11 SEP 2026 9:35PM by PIB Delhi

Drydocks World, a DP World company, and Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL) today announced the signing of a joint venture agreement to operate and expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) Cochin.

The agreement was signed by Captain Rado Antolovic, PhD, CEO, Drydocks World, and Mr. Jose V J, Chairman & Managing Director of Cochin Shipyard Ltd., on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, in the presence of Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), and H.E. Omran Sharaf Alhashimi, UAE Assistant Foreign Minister for Advanced Science and Technology.

The agreement builds on the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by Drydocks World (DDW) and CSL during India Maritime Week 2025, under which the two organizations agreed to explore opportunities for collaboration in ship repair and allied maritime services. The companies have now formalised this collaboration through a 50:50 joint venture, marking the establishment of a first-of-its-kind public-private partnership in India’s ship repair sector.

Under the arrangement, the joint venture will operate, consolidate and expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) in Cochin, creating additional capacity to service a wider range of vessels and meet the growing requirements of Indian, regional and international customers.

The partnership is expected to strengthen Cochin’s position as a maritime services hub, while creating opportunities across ship repair, engineering, fabrication and associated maritime services in Kerala.

Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, said: “The partnership between Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World marks an important milestone in strengthening India’s ship repair ecosystem and reflects the enduring maritime relationship between India and the UAE, which has flourished through centuries of trade, commerce and people-to-people ties. The shared vision and resolve of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan are giving a new momentum to this relationship across strategic and economic sectors. By combining India’s growing shipbuilding and ship repair capabilities with the UAE’s global maritime expertise, this joint venture will create new capacity, skills and economic opportunities, while strengthening Cochin as a maritime services hub. Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is firmly on course to emerge as one of the world’s leading maritime nations, and this partnership is another step towards realising that ambition under Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.”

His Excellency Omran Sharaf Alhashimi, Assistant Foreign Minister for Advanced Science and Technology, UAE, said, “The UAE and India share a longstanding relationship rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and a common ambition to create new pathways for growth. The joint venture between Drydocks World and Cochin Shipyard is a strong example of how this partnership can translate into tangible industrial outcomes, bringing together complementary expertise to strengthen India’s maritime capabilities. By combining India’s growing maritime potential with the UAE’s global experience, collaborations such as this can support more efficient ship repair services, strengthen maritime connectivity and contribute to the continued growth of trade and commerce between our two countries.”

Vijay Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways said, “This Joint Venture shall not be limited to Kochi. It is a replicable model that can be extended across India’s extensive coastline, creating hubs of excellence in ship repair and conversion. By leveraging India’s strategic location and proximity to global trade routes, the JV will attract foreign investments, generate foreign exchange, and create thousands of skilled jobs. It will also align with the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, positioning India as a global powerhouse in ship building and ship repair. The signing of this Joint Venture Agreement is more than a business agreement, it is a statement of intent. It signals India’s readiness to compete globally, deliver world-class maritime services, and forge partnerships that strengthen our economy and strategic capabilities.”

Captain Rado Antolovic, PhD, CEO, Drydocks World, said: “This partnership with Cochin Shipyard is an important milestone for India’s ship repair industry and builds on the strong foundation of our MoU last year. By combining Cochin Shipyard’s local expertise and skilled workforce with Drydocks World’s global capabilities and technology, we are creating a world-class ship repair offering. Our ambition goes beyond one facility - we see opportunities to expand ship repair and fabrication capabilities across India.”

Jose V J, Chairman and Managing Director, Cochin Shipyard Ltd., said: “This joint venture with Drydocks World Dubai marks a defining moment in India’s journey to become a global ship repair hub. By combining CSL’s deep domestic experience with DDW’s world-class expertise, we are not just scaling up business - we are onboarding global best practices, accelerating turnaround times, and setting new benchmarks for quality and safety. Anchored at the International Ship Repair Facility in Kochi, this partnership will catalyse a thriving repair cluster, attract international fleets, generate high-skilled employment, and advance the vision of Maritime India 2030 and Amrit Kaal 2047.”

The partnership combines CSL’s established shipbuilding and repair capabilities, engineering expertise and skilled workforce with Drydocks World’s global experience in high-end vessel repair and maintenance, major conversions, and offshore engineering, procurement and construction (EPC). Strategically located along major international shipping routes, the facility features a state-of-the-art ship lift system and modern docking facilities capable of servicing a wide range of vessels.

Drydocks World and Cochin Shipyard Ltd. will each hold a 50% stake, with initial capital funded through equity contributions from both parties.

(Release ID: 2309337)

  - CSL’s Managing Director, Jose V J, noted the venture will set benchmarks for quality, safety, and turnaround times while catalyzing a repair cluster in Cochin.  
  - Drydocks World CEO Rado Antolovic stated the partnership combines local expertise with global capabilities to build a world-class ship repair offering.

headline: Prime Minister meets with UN Secretary-General on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister meets with UN Secretary-General on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit

11 SEP 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today met with the UN Secretary-General, H.E. Mr. António Guterres, on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

UNSG Guterres congratulated PM Modi for India’s chairship of the BRICS for the fourth time. Both leaders underscored the significance of multipolarity and the need to reform multilateral institutions, including the UN Security Council, to reflect contemporary realities.

They also held discussions on various issues, including ongoing conflicts and freedom of navigation, sustainable development, human-centric AI, progress in renewable energy, and global food security.

PM Modi wished UNSG Guterres the very best for the remainder of his tenure.

(Release ID: 2309334)

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi met with UN Secretary-General H.E. Mr. António Guterres on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where both leaders discussed global governance reform, multipolarity, and a range of pressing international issues.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- The meeting took place on 11 September 2026, as part of the BRICS Summit held in New Delhi.
- UNSG Guterres congratulated PM Modi for India's chairship of the BRICS for the fourth time.
